corrections.text: The article states, citing the Nature Geoscience paper, that wide flank uplifts fade within roughly 15 to 100 million years and that 'three named rift systems — Ganis, Dali, and Devana Chasmata — show topography consistent with tectonic extension,' and separately that the simulations were 'built around a 150-kilometer-thick thermal lithosphere and three different crustal compositions.' The Nature Geoscience source (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41561-026-02044-8) was inaccessible to editorial review — both the archived snapshot and a live re-fetch redirected to an idp.nature.com authentication wall with no visible abstract or article text — and the accessible Phys.org source does not contain these figures either. These specific details could not be independently verified at the time of publication.
